M-O s.v. screw

cōchlea / cochlea, -ae f.

noun, first declension

Ancient cochlea already denotes spiral and screw mechanisms; later technical Latin applies it directly to the modern threaded fastener. Lewis & Short marks the first vowel of cochlea as variable (cō̆-), so this lexicon does not pretend that one quantity is uniquely correct. The modern English distinction between screw and bolt is not mapped consistently onto one fixed pair of Latin nouns in the sources checked; cochlea is therefore kept broad here rather than creating a false precision. Modern Latin sources do not maintain a single universally standardized terminology for every modern screwdriver, screw and wrench subtype; specific types should therefore be formed or selected case by case.

Examples

  • Cochleam vertitōriō intorque.

    Screw the screw in with the screwdriver.composed

See also screwdriver, nut, screw thread, screw in, unscrew.

SourcesLewis & Short: coclea / cochlea · Morgan–Owens: screw
